FLY TYING / BEGINNERS

How to tie an Elk Hair Caddis

One fly, eight clear steps. Gather the materials, follow each stage, and check the finished shape before you start the next one.

Castward field notes Updated 11 November 2026
At a glance
Pattern
Elk Hair Caddis
Lesson
8 illustrated steps
Goal
Secure wraps • clear eye
Start here

Quick answer

Take one stage at a time. Keep the hook eye clear, use only the material the step needs, and check each tie-in before you move on.

On this page

  1. Lay out the materials
  2. Tie it, one step at a time
  3. Your finished fly

  5. Common questions

01

Lay out the materials

These sizes are a starting recipe. Test the hook and materials together before you tie a batch.[1]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

PartFor this version
HookSize 14 dry-fly hook
ThreadTan 70 denier
RibFine gold wire
BodyTan dry-fly dubbing
HackleBrown dry-fly feather
WingCleaned elk hair
02

Tie it, one step at a time

  1. 01

    Start with thread and wire

    Cover the shank with tan thread. Tie in fine gold wire, leaving its free end at the bend.

    Bench tip Keep a clear space behind the eye.

  2. 02

    Dub a slim body

    Twist a small pinch of dubbing onto the thread. Wrap a tapered tan body toward the eye.

    Bench tip Use less dubbing than you expect.

  3. 03

    Tie in the hackle

    Secure the bare feather stem at the front of the body.

    Bench tip Match the hackle to the hook size.

  4. 04

    Palmer toward the bend

    Wind the hackle rearward in open turns. Trap its tip with the wire at the bend.

    Bench tip Palmer means wind the feather along the body.

  5. 05

    Lock the hackle

    Spiral the wire forward through the hackle. Secure it; remove excess wire and feather.

    Bench tip Wiggle the wire between the fibers.

  6. 06

    Prepare the wing

    Clean a small elk-hair bunch. Align the tips in a stacker and measure them to the hook bend.

    Bench tip Remove the soft underfur first.

  7. 07

    Secure the elk hair

    Hold the bunch on top. Make loose collecting wraps, tighten, and trim the butts into a short head.

    Bench tip Hold the wing to prevent it rolling.

  8. 08

    Make the finish

    Whip finish under the hair head. Cut the thread and clear the eye.

    Bench tip Check that the wing does not spin.

[1]
03

Your finished fly

  • ✓The hook eye stays clear.
  • ✓The materials stay put under a gentle tug.
  • ✓The point and hook gap remain usable.
04

Small mistakes, simple fixes

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

What you seeTry this
A wing that rollsHold the hair on top while you tighten.
A long wingMeasure the tips to the bend before you tie in.
A buried hook eyeUse a smaller bunch and a shorter head.
A few good questions

Before you head out

Can I change the color?

Yes. Keep the same sequence and use comparable materials. Change one feature at a time so you can see its effect.

What if the fly looks uneven?

Check the secure wraps and open eye first. Keep this fly as a reference, then repeat the recipe with less material.
